data.reasoning: The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD and found it to follow standard Arch packaging practices with no malicious code. The .SRCINFO confirms all sources and patches are pinned with SHA-256 checksums. While both models incorrectly skipped the patch files (misidentifying them as binary), these are local files with verified checksums and their names indicate benign build system adjustments (install path fixes for KDE/GNOME). The qwen3-235b inconclusive result was due to API errors, not security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool failures rather than security analysis. qwen3-235b returned 'inconclusive' because HTTP 400 errors prevented it from reviewing the PKGBUILD and .gitignore. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed these files and found them safe. Both models shared the same failure mode of incorrectly skipping patch files.
coverage_issues: Both models incorrectly skipped patch files (0001-cmake-Install-kde-wallpaper-to-correct-path.patch, 0002-cmake-Install-gnome-extensions-separately.patch) by misidentifying them as binary files. Patches are text files applied during prepare() and must be reviewed.
qwen3-235b failed to review PKGBUILD and .gitignore due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), leaving critical files unaudited.
false_negatives: Patch files were not reviewed by either model. While their names suggest benign build adjustments and they are checksum-pinned, patches execute during prepare() and could theoretically contain malicious commands if the maintainer compromised them.
learnings: File type detection must correctly identify .patch files as text, not binary. The current logic incorrectly skips them, creating a critical coverage gap for files that execute during build.
Implement retry logic or fallback models when API errors occur to prevent incomplete audits of critical files like PKGBUILD.
Prioritize review of all files referenced in PKGBUILD functions (especially patches in prepare()), regardless of file extension heuristics.
